references.text: The context for the design of the lampstand, including the placement of the knobs and the six branches extending from the central shaft.
Continuation of the description of the knobs and branches, which are to be made of one piece with the lampstand, of pure gold.
Bezalel carries out the construction of the lampstand with knobs beneath each pair of branches, as commanded in chapter 25.
Description of the lampstand's craftsmanship in hammered gold, from its base to the flowers, according to the pattern shown by the Lord to Moses.
Zechariah's vision of a golden lampstand with seven lamps, connecting to the tabernacle's lampstand and its symbolic meaning.
John sees seven golden lampstands in his vision, based on the symbolism from the tabernacle's lampstand.
This verse confirms that the lampstand was made in full accordance with God's specific instructions given earlier.
Both verses highlight the complex and symbolic nature of the lampstand by combining descriptions of buds, branches, cups, and flowers.
This verse establishes the structural framework (six branches) that makes the placement of the six buds in the source verse possible.
Connects the construction description to its function: the lampstand was built this way to fulfill the purpose of shining forward.
